description.narrative:
Stakeholder effects: The Project increases availability of drinking water in the MGC. The Project supports municipal investments by EMPAGUA, including the construction of greenfield Water Treatment Plants (WTP) and the rehabilitation of the infrastructure network in Guatemala City. These investments will optimize the use of surface water and provide an alternative to alleviate exploited groundwater resources. IFC expects these investments to add capacity to treat drinking water, which will increase the volume of drinking water supplied to MGC. Hence, benefiting users with improved potable water availability (50 l/day) and resilience to climate change vulnerabilities.
Environmental effects: The Project is expected to treat contaminated surface water to address water scarcity and climate change vulnerabilities. In this sense, the Project provides a short-term solution to preserve critical surface water resources under stress and secure a more stable water production that is less sensitive to climate change. The Project supports the construction of greenfield WTPs, which will add capacity to treat surface contaminated water. This will enable EMPAGUA to treat contaminated surface water in Guatemala City, which would become available for reuse in a water scarce context. Hence, improving the availability of treated drinking water sources to adapt to the stress of climate-driven drought in the short-term, while the municipality develops integral long-term solutions to holistically address water scarcity.

The project entails financing to the Municipality of Guatemala City (MGC) to address the citys infrastructure bottlenecks by funding capital expenditures in (1) water infrastructure, such as small greenfield water treatment plants (WTP), as well as the rehabilitation and expansion of an existing groundwater extraction facility managed by the municipal water company EMPAGUA; (2) modernizing the citys traffic light system through the installation of smart traffic lights and associated software and infrastructure upgrades to the existing control center, managed by the MGCs Regulatory Entity for Transportation and Traffic - EMETRA and (3) assessing the feasibility of installing urban cycling routes and the deployment of a public bicycle system, managed by the Department of Urban Mobility, Planning Management of the MGC (together, the Project).
